description: Retrieval eval cases (memory phase G). Every case runs against corpus.json with `now` fixed, so results are deterministic and no LLM is called - which means this set runs in the ordinary test suite rather than costing API quota like the extraction eval.
scoring_note: Resolution and citations are scored separately on purpose. A case can resolve the right filter and still cite the wrong spans, and the two failures have different causes - a parser bug versus an index bug. Collapsing them into one number would hide which.

cases.question: what did I commit to yesterday

texts: I will send the investor deck tonight

cases.note: The 24th. Must not return the hostel form from the 21st.

cases.question: what did we decide on Saturday
cases.note: Saturday is the 21st, which has a suggestion and a commitment but no decision. The important half is the direction: resolving Saturday FORWARD to the 28th would also return nothing, and would look identical. The time_label assertion is what distinguishes them.

cases.question: what did we decide last week

texts: We decided to go with the Groq provider for now

cases.note: Mon 16th to Sun 22nd, so the 16th decision is in and the 24th pricing decision is out.

cases.question: what did we talk about at the academic block
cases.note: Place names come from places actually recorded, so the match is case-insensitive against the stored label.

cases.question: what did we decide at Blue Tokai

texts: We decided the pricing stays at nineteen ninety

cases.note: Two constraints narrowing to one span out of three at that place. The query session-grained retrieval could not express.

cases.question: what has Pulkit committed to
cases.note: Resolution only. Citations are NOT asserted: nothing populates `speaker_person_id` yet, so the person filter resolves and cannot narrow. That gap is the point of participant labelling, and this case is what will start passing citations when it lands.

cases.question: what did pull kit promise
cases.note: Whisper's mis-hearing must resolve to the same person. This is phase B's squash rule reached through the question parser.

cases.question: what do I owe
cases.note: Owing spans commitment, assignment and requirement, so it is a flag rather than a single act. A case that asserted acts == ['commitment'] would lock in the wrong model.

cases.question: did I ever mention the exam

texts: The exam timetable came out this morning

cases.question: how many times did I promise something
cases.note: The scaffolding must not leak into the text filter. 'how many' once left 'many' behind and the filter started matching on it.

cases.question: what did we decide that day
cases.note: Asks rather than guessing. A guessed range returns real sentences from the wrong moment, which reads as an answer rather than a mistake.

cases.question: what happened
cases.note: Admitted, not forced. Silently matching on stopwords would return the whole corpus.

cases.question: what did we decide about the budget
cases.note: An honest empty, and the verdict must name the filter so a badly-phrased question is distinguishable from an empty history.

cases.question: what did anyone suggest

texts: Priya suggested we move the review to next week

cases.note: Base verb forms matter: 'suggest' was missing from the act table while 'suggested' was present, and this case is what caught it.

cases.question: what was Pulkit supposed to do
what did I commit to at Blue Tokai yesterday

texts: I will send the investor deck tonight

cases.note: Four constraints at once. The single most important case in the set: it is the shape of the question the whole memory plan exists to answer.
